title: Keeping young, health and why Palmer stopped playing
summary: Chat on looking young, not drinking, avoiding worry, and why he quit.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: He's such a friendly fellow. What is his address? I don't know for sure. I have it at home. I'll try to find it. Yeah? I'll make a note of it right now. Yeah. I have it at home. Unless he's moved. I haven't seen him for about six or seven years. I see. Well, he was supposed to come here this winter. There was one trumpet player, a white kid, who had a band. And when he left Ory, he was going to get him to come here in June. But Garland didn't come with him. Oh, I guess. Maybe June. Because he didn't want to travel. Yeah. So I'll look up his address. If I don't know it, this kid I know, this trumpet player could tell me where he lives. And some other friends I have out there, too. I see. He always looked well and looked as young. Like David said, there's nobody that's as young as you. How do you do it? Do you know it? He'll look just as young as I was 30 years old. I heard something in 1940. That's 50 years ago. Same thing.

What do you do? Well, take care of yourself. You know, man, don't run around too much and getting drunk, laying out in the snow. That ain't no good. No, that's true. I saw some nice musicians. I had to clap. It was a shame. You haven't lost your hair, no gray hair or anything? No. Well, that's just to keep up. See? I don't drink at all. I lost all of my hair. Well, some people do lose their hair early, you know. Yeah, that's right. And a lot of people just keep their hair a long time before they, you know, travel. Yeah, I never worry about nothing. But if you get to worry, you're going to get a whole inch over. I see fellows around my age out of the crowd. I just feel sorry for them.
Yeah, I feel sorry for them.

All of a sudden they go to pieces. Yeah, all to pieces. And it seems like they worry a lot, you know, about, you know, I used to worry about nothing. And eat plenty. Do like you and me. Get your food and have a nice meal. And don't run out and get drunk and all that stuff. Laying out in the snow. That's bad. Yeah, if you take care of yourself, it's better. That's the better, you know, because even so, man, I have a million years to live in. You just might as well enjoy it and take, you know, do the best of it you can, see. I didn't quit trombone, stop playing trombone because it was too hard for me or, you know, anything like that. The only thing I quit, it wasn't no work, Russell. No, that's right. It wasn't no work. I'd rather go to work than to do like a lot of those guys, get out and get to stealing and robbing and, you know.
